title: Enterprise admin request escalation and priority playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: define a concrete escalation and prioritization playbook for enterprise admin and access requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policies) that complements the intake framework. Scope includes intake routing, triage scoring, SLA targets, communication templates, and on-call escalation paths. Excludes implementation engineering work (covered under Dedicated/ENG tickets) and low-touch self-serve UI improvements which remain in the intake backlog.
triage_rubric_summary: Generate a 0-10 priority score combining customer impact, security/regulatory risk, business revenue/time-to-value, and operational effort. Tier mapping: 8-10 = P0 (SLA: 48h start, dedicated owner), 5-7 = P1 (SLA: 5 business days), 2-4 = P2 (SLA: 2 sprints), 0-1 = P3 (queued for intake).
escalation_matrix: Tier 1: Support triage -> PM review within SLA. Tier 2: PM escalation to Access program lead -> schedule architecture/eng review. Tier 3: Exec escalation for legal/regulatory blocking issues. Include on-call rotation for enterprise access issues for 24/7 coverage during major outages or security incidents.
sla_targets: P0: acknowledge within 2 hours, begin work within 48 hours; P1: acknowledge within 8 business hours, begin investigations within 5 business days; P2: acknowledge within 3 business days; P3: acknowledge within 7 business days.
scoring_criteria: Customer impact: number of affected org seats and revenue exposure (0-4)
Security/regulatory risk: SAML assertion issues, SCIM provisioning failures, audit log gaps (0-3)
Operational blast radius: cross-tenant risk or platform-wide regression (0-2)
Implementation complexity: estimated eng days and infra changes (0-1)
sample_routing_rules: SSO/SAML failures (login outages) => route to identity-specialist queue + PM immediate review
SCIM provisioning mismatches (user sync) => route to provisioning queue + request customer manifest and logs
RBAC policy change requests that impact >=5 orgs => escalate to Access program lead for architecture review
Org-level policy enforcement requests (data residency, KMS access) => require security review flag and legal notification
communication_templates: Initial ack: 'Thanks for filing — we've triaged this and assigned a priority of P{n}. Owner: {assignee}. Next update within {SLA}.'
Escalation to customer: 'We're escalating this to our access engineering team and will provide a rollout plan within 48 hours.'
Closure note: 'Issue resolved. Root cause: {summary}. Rollout notes: {steps}. If you see recurrence please reopen.'
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence and linked from intake form
Support routing rules implemented in Linear/Helpdesk mapping and tested with 3 sample requests
On-call rotation defined and added to PagerDuty with runbook links
Communication templates added to canned responses and internal handbook
implementation_steps: Draft playbook and get PM + security review sign-off
Update intake form to capture triage fields (impact score, regulatory tag, customer SLA) and enforce required fields for identity-related tickets
Configure Linear workflows: labels, auto-assign rules, and SLAs based on rubric
Add PagerDuty on-call rotation & link runbook; test by simulating a P0 SSO outage
Train Support and Solutions on routing and templates; hold 30-min cross-functional sync
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: inconsistent scoring between reviewers -> Mitigation: include two-reviewer consensus for P0/P1 and sample scoring examples
Risk: delayed eng capacity for P0 -> Mitigation: pre-approved war-room capacity and runbook for quick rollback to previous ACLs
Risk: customer confusion over SLAs -> Mitigation: public-facing SLA summary and transparent status page updates
